title.en: FDM print layers and perimeter-start seams

summary: Separate layer stepping and perimeter-start marks from paint or random damage when depicting an extrusion-printed part.
objective: Separate layer stepping and perimeter-start marks from paint or random damage when depicting an extrusion-printed part.
intent_signals: Separate layer stepping and perimeter-start marks from paint or random damage when depicting an extrusion-printed part.
example_prompts: Build an explorable fdm print layers and perimeter-start seams and expose its construction at close range.

principles: Choose a declared build direction and perimeter strategy. A layer band, a start/end seam and a scratch are different features; distribute them according to that construction instead of applying isotropic noise.
The source explicitly exempts spiral-vase mode from ordinary perimeter start/end seams. Do not paint a vertical seam onto every possible extrusion-print process.
implementation: Store a local build axis, authored layer height, seam placement policy and finish state with the part. Use a simple constant-layer teaching preset; do not present it as parsed toolpath data. Layer bands follow build height even when the finished object is rotated in the scene.

On a curved test shell depict finite layer stepping where it changes silhouette; use small normal/roughness variation for unresolved bead detail elsewhere. Preserve modeled wall thickness and actual openings independently of the shading pattern.

Place local start/end marks at the declared perimeter positions. Compare aligned and scattered placements as authored examples; do not equate random seam placement with random pits everywhere or claim a particular strength gain.

Top and bottom faces have their own authored line layout rather than repeating sidewall bands. A sanded or coated preset can reduce visible microdetail; keep that finish separate from the underlying shape and label any explanatory uncoated inset.

At overview scale merge unresolved layer marks into a stable surface response. At close range retain a few coherent seam and bead transitions without requiring every filament strand to be a mesh. Offer a build-axis overlay, seam highlight and finish toggle.
observable_checks: Rotate the object: layer orientation follows its manufacturing frame, not the camera or world up.
Switch aligned to scattered seam positions: layer height, shell dimensions and openings stay unchanged; only the authored start/end locations change.
Compare sidewall, sloped silhouette and top surface at two distances; no exaggerated displacement closes a hole or turns fine layers into structural ribs.

known_limits: No slicer execution, G-code validation, actual printability, interlayer strength, porosity or calibrated polymer optics. Spiral-vase, variable layers and scarf seams need separately specified depiction.
Authored construction and prospective checks; no runtime artifact, render or material test has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Use a rough prototype, smooth finished product or exaggerated teaching closeup; a refined print need not visibly advertise every layer.

claims.statement: Prusa explains that ordinary perimeter loops start and end at a location that can create a visible seam, distinguishes seam placement options, and identifies spiral-vase mode as an exception.
claims.scope: Perimeter-based FFF/FDM seam explanation; no universal seam visibility or material-strength guarantee.

source_refs.locator: Opening explanation; Seam Position subsections Aligned and Random; final Vase mode exception
